tests.skip_reason: Opt-in desktop X11 passive-viewer test requires MINE_UAV_GUI_TEST=1; not needed for offline dynamics experiment.
tests.scope: Current branch tracked test files plus this experiment's new test module; unrelated pre-existing untracked historical-branch tests excluded.
tests.read_only_verification: All 8 checks pass: immutable hashes, matched start identities, same initialization, normalization, validation selection/loss, all frozen/new Test metrics and unchanged yaw conventions.

research_assessment.horizon_hypothesis: Supported for aggregate 25/50-step prediction in this single-seed objective-matched comparison; not uniform improvement at all horizons/dimensions.
research_assessment.loss_scaling_confound: Removed for matched K1 versus existing K10: identical saved observation std, architecture, random initialization, Adam configuration, start identities and batch order rule. Only prediction horizon differs; validation uses each prescribed horizon.
research_assessment.h50_horizon_effect: Matched K1 normalized RMSE 0.29601142497 versus K10 0.24231579130: 18.1397% reduction, beyond the 10-step training horizon.
research_assessment.historical_attribution_limit: No exact fraction of the historical 13.34% gain is assigned to horizon/scaling. Historical delta-loss K1 additionally included terminal-tail starts; its A-to-B contrast is not a pure scaling-only intervention. Matched K1 did not reproduce that aggregate long-horizon gain.
research_assessment.dimension_tradeoff: At H50, K10 versus matched K1 improves horizontal velocity RMSE 16.8469% and yaw 43.4138%, while vz RMSE worsens 4.2136%; error_z also worsens. K10 yaw remains 121.72% worse than historical delta-loss K1, so horizon alone does not explain historical yaw regression.
research_assessment.yaw_correctness: Original wrapped observation and raw-coordinate prediction/error conventions retained. No adjacent wrap jumps in Train/Val/Test. No yaw-loss or representation change.
research_assessment.next_recommendation_only: A separately authorized latent-transition formulation is reasonable, retaining multivariable loss balance and short/vertical-horizon tradeoffs. Nothing beyond this control experiment was executed.

generation_config.input_convention: pre-command obs7 + previous executed normalized action4

dataset.transition_rule: o_t=inputs[t,:7], a_t=actions[t], next=inputs[t+1,:7]; within episode only
dataset.previous_action_rule: inputs[t,7:11] = executed normalized action at t-1; reset=0

windows.protocol: all starts t in range(max(0,N-H+1)), per episode

training.optimizer: Adam defaults (betas=.9,.999 eps=1e-8), no gradient clipping
training.warmup_gradient_rule: differentiable true prefix, no prefix loss; all K prediction steps fully connected

objective: mean ((predicted next physical observation - recorded next observation)/saved Train observation std)^2; K=1, same loss family/scale as K10
output_parameterization: same saved delta mean/std inverse transform at the head; NOT the loss weighting
start_matching: K1 uses exact original K10 starts; causal prefix slices end after last used start; source trajectories unchanged
protocol: current observation + previous executed normalized action -> GRU prefix; recorded current actions; no true PI input

pi_magnitude_bins.rule: Train transition PI norm tertiles; small<q1, q1<=medium<q2, large>=q2

limitations: Single seed and nominal recorded-action trajectories; not policy/planning evaluation.
Validation uses each condition's own prescribed horizon; no Test checkpoint selection.
Historical delta-loss K1 additionally used terminal-tail starts: A-to-B is not a clean scaling-only intervention.
K1-to-K10 holds start identities fixed, but future horizon labels and optimization trajectory differ by design.
No additive causal percentage decomposition of the historical improvement; dimension-level tradeoffs require separate interpretation.
Yaw remains the original wrapped observation coordinate; prediction/evaluation use unchanged raw coordinate differences.
